questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I thought Paris was a really interesting city and that the academic opportunities at Sciences Po were interesting as well.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was really happy with my time in Paris.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was relatively easy. Sometimes I needed to seeke out the information myself but the people at Sciences Po are really helpful.

questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through cite universitare were I applied through Fondation Danoise and received a room at Fondation Hellenique.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was really nice living at the cite universitare. I would recommend applying early on through fondation danoise - I applied in September and was told in October that I had gotten a room, so that saved me from a lot of housing stress early on.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process was fine but the course registration process is stressful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get access to a website with all the courses at the same time as all other students and then the courses gets filled up really quick. I was lucky that I got some courses that I was really happy with. But I got none of the courses that I initially thought I would get. I can recommend checking the site multiple times through the night while it is still open - some courses got available later on and then I could shift some of my courses with some more interesting ones.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There wasn't really any help with the course registration. It is possible to participate in a zoom meeting before the registration where they introduce and talk about the process. And I think it was also possible to get and shift courses in the first to weeks of the semester.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was lucky that I got interesting courses but the weren't the ones I initially wanted. I think most of the courses will turn out to be exciting when you turn up on the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: see the advice above about the registration above.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was happy with my courses and teachers.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the academic level was fine - the readings and content of the courses reminded me of the level at UCPH. There was a lot of projects and presentations each week and a lot of group work which can be frustrating. But the semester is really short and already ends in May - So I think the academic burden is worth it. And the exams were fine as well - they are written in hand which is a bit different from what I was used to, but the exams were not too difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: My courses reminded a lot of the style of teaching at UCPH. The students are included a bit more and expected to be active participants - but that also differs from course to course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL GOVERNANCE: POWER, POLITICS AND THE PLANET (NEW COURSE) 
FISCAL AND SOCIAL POLICIES IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES: RESEARCH AND PRACTICE 
DEMOCRACY, PARTIES AND ELECTIONS IN EUROPE Emiliano GROSSMAN 
DIGITAL AND AI-RELATED CHALLENGES AT THE CROSSROADS OF CULTURE, ECONOMICS AND POLITICS Carlo SANTAGIUSTINA 
EUROPE'S COMING OF AGE. CAN THE EU BECOME A GLOBAL ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL ACTOR? Loukas TSOUKALIS

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recommend the course 58549 DEMOCRACY, PARTIES AND ELECTIONS IN EUROPE with Emiliano GROSSMAN - really nice introduction to the themes off political science. And the course 57354  FISCAL AND SOCIAL POLICIES IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES: RESEARCH AND PRACTICE with Justine KNEBELMANN. Both teachers are really good and the content is interesting.

questions.answer: both sports and social clubs I think.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not participate in any so I cant recommend any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just all of Paris. It is a lovely city with so much opportunities. The cultural offers are really nice so go to the museums. the restaurants are lovely and the parks as well. And then it is of course really nice to travel to other cities in France. I went to Séte which was really nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was really easy. I dont think the language barrier is as big as people say - most people spoke good English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No unfortunately not. Maybe through student groups in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the fact that people use the city a lot. The French are always out on the streets and sitting at cafes. I really loved how alive the city is.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Apply at cite universitare for living.
Be open to get other courses than you expected.
and look forward to it because Paris is amazing

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the most rewarding part was just living in Paris.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was beginning at a new institution. Sciences po was nice but change is always difficult in the beginning
